b: I’m 24F and I’ve been very close with two friends, N and M (both also 24F) , for years. This weekend I was staying with them and we were just chatting for ages as we do until they mentioned something I didn’t recognise. I pushed them to explain, and this is what came out.

A mutual friend, L, used to date a Black guy. (I am also black for context)After they broke up, L had a serious breakdown, that landed her being admitted into hospital and her mum ended up blaming the relationship fallout on Black people and told her not to hang out with them (she has grown up in a strict religious upbringing and tends to take her mums words as gospel). Two years ago we were all meant to go to Leicester for N’s birthday, L was supposed to drive, and she told N and M she couldn’t drive me because her mum had told her not to spend time with Black people. I’m Black.
N and M cut L off for a month or two. She apologised after some time and said she was ashamed of what she’d said, and they started talking to her again. They never told me. They’d decided between themselves that it would be too hard for me to hear, and that they were “protecting me.” If I hadn’t noticed the reference this weekend, they’ve said they never would have. I know this because of the way it came up, M blurted out “Do you remember when we fell out with L over the car thing?” and N was like you idiot why did you say that and then I had to literally pressure them into telling me.
I’m not that close with L, and as soon as I found out I removed her from everything, so she isn’t really the issue. What’s upsetting me is N and M. We’ve talked about it since and they’ve explained their reasoning, but I still feel annoyed and I’m struggling to believe “we were protecting you” is the whole story. They took it seriously enough to cut L off, so they clearly knew it was a big deal. Two years is a long time to sit on something that directly involved me.
I don’t want to kill the vibe or blow up the friendship, and I know they probably meant well. But it makes me feel like they decided what I could handle without asking me, and I know I’d never do that to them.
Why am I still upset? How do I move past this, or do I need to say something more to them?
EDIT: they are south asian not white
